title: inventory/1 — <artifacts>/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-inventory.json
description: Wave 0's single machine-readable inventory: one item per open item of the board, every survey and every harvested source (references/waves.md, Wave 0). scripts/waves.py merges audit outputs into it (`merge`), writes `module`, `node`, `wave` and `release` from two short tables (`assign`), counts it (`count`) and refuses an item that lands nowhere (`validate`). The document is an object carrying `schema` and `items`; a bare array of items is read as the items of one. Fields a project needs beyond these go under an `x-` prefix.

id.description: The item's id in its owning register. An item without one gets one there, in the same change. Unique across the inventory.

area.description: The part of the system it touches.

kind.description: What sort of item: e.g. bug, gap, weak-impl, contradiction, doc-wrong, doc-missing, plan.

evidence.description: The receipt: file:line at a commit, or a command and its output. A finding is a fact with a receipt, never an impression.

status.description: As measured, not as the register last said. Absent means open. Every value but open and changed is terminal; carried means release program with a reason.

source.description: Where it was found, when that differs from the evidence: a register row as file:line, or the command that surfaced it.

source_file.description: The survey output it was merged from (written by `waves.py merge`).

module.description: The dossier cluster it belongs to (written by `waves.py assign` from the module table).

node.description: The canvas nodes that close it, in wave order (written by `waves.py assign` from the plan's `closes`).

wave.description: The wave that closes it: the last wave among its nodes. Null when it is carried to a later release.

modules.description: The module table `assign --modules` reads: module name -> the item ids it holds. An id in two modules is refused. Edited as the canvas is cut; a re-cut is a diff to this table.

plan.description: The wave plan `assign --plan` and `sync-graph` read: any JSON whose `nodes` lists {id, wave, closes}. A work graph that carries `closes` on its nodes is one. A node whose wave is not an integer is carried (`release: program`).

graph_id.description: The work-graph node this canvas node is built as, where the two ids differ; `sync-graph` moves that node.

risk.description: The node's risk class; `sync-graph` writes it onto the work-graph node (a lowering needs --lower-why), and `graph.py close` enforces the rounds it owes.
